financial_anchor.metric: H1 2026 turnover, GAAP operating profit and underlying operating profit
financial_anchor.caveat: Underlying operating profit is non-GAAP; reported operating profit is GAAP. The materiality screen below uses GAAP.

ai_claim.claim: Unilever reports AI-supported demand and supply forecasting and a Raeford factory using digital twins for quality and throughput; it plans more than 40 AI-powered digital twins over 18 months.
ai_claim.stage: E2 issuer-reported named production use at Raeford; wider rollout E1; no E3/E4
ai_claim.scope: Raeford digital-twin production and supply-chain forecasting; planned network rollout remains separate.
ai_claim.limitation: No baseline, quantified Raeford outcome, model-cost allocation, matched cohort or retained-cash reconciliation.

strongest_counterevidence.claim: commodity/input inflation and pricing response dominate margins.
strongest_counterevidence.limitation: Does not itself disprove the scoped mechanism.

rights_limit: Public terms do not prove universal training or pooled cross-customer reuse; enterprise schedules were unavailable.
materiality_summary: €245m = 5% of H1 2026 GAAP operating profit of €4.9bn. This is a six-month, pre-tax screen and is NOT_COMPARABLE with the annual benefit illustration; no annualization is assumed.

arithmetic.inputs: pool €12bn eligible supply-chain, marketing-production and support cost; efficiency 10%; realization 40%; retained share 50%; recurring cost €150m
arithmetic.formula: eligible cost × efficiency × realization × retained share − recurring AI expense

g2_provisional: Watch/incomplete: E1 supply-chain capability; no opened controlled cohort; no E3 quality-adjusted proof or E4 retained cash.
unresolved_questions: Eligible workload and matched quality KPI?
